title and abstract.summary: This study assessed the morphological traits of beetles and ants across four different biotopes in Table Mountain National Park to evaluate how the functional trait composition of these insect groups responds to passive restoration following the removal of invasive pine.

methods.summary: The study measured various traits (body length, dispersal ability, color, pilosity, number of spines) and calculated functional diversity metrics for groups of beetles and ants across different biotopes.

results.summary: The study measured traits such as body size, dispersal potential, color, hairiness, and spine numbers for 45 species of beetles and 21 species of ants across different biotopes. The study measured functional richness, functional dispersion, and RaoQ for various groups of beetles and ants across different biotopes (pine, new recovering fynbos, old recovering fynbos, and pristine fynbos), but it did not specify the individual species whose traits or measurements were analyzed.
